A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Discrete Transformer research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison despite restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original training/test losses, extracted programs, annealing dynamics, and architectural intervention results in Tables 1–2, Figures 2–8, and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original training losses, extracted-program accuracy/RMSE, continuous-dynamics results, and capacity analyses. The separately attributed MIPS results do not affect this assessment.

M1.justification: The scalar residual stream, Numerical Attention, sub-MLPs, annealed selection, and hypothesis-testing/PySR extraction pipeline remain unchanged. Pruning remains in Section 4.3 after its duplicate explanation is removed from Section 3.4. Newly specified implementation details do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Tables 1–2 expand coverage from 17 to 26 tasks, retaining the original tasks and adding div_3, magnetic, unique_prev2, parity_zeros, bit_dot_prod_mod_2, bit_addition, balanced_parenthesis, exponential_moving_average, and free_fall_height. This substantially extends symbolic task requirements and explicitly evaluated floating-point dynamics.

E2.justification: V1 discusses MIPS qualitatively but tabulates only Discrete Transformer losses. V2 makes MIPS an explicit quantitative comparator throughout Table 1, using published accuracy results and marking unsuccessful or inapplicable cases. These are attributed prior results, not newly reported MIPS runs.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes from model test MSE to reported extracted-program evaluation using nearest-integer accuracy and RMSE; floating-point tasks receive RMSE only. This changes the documented evaluation target and scoring procedure. Shared training settings in Appendix C remain unchanged, while added tasks receive corresponding model configurations.

E4.justification: V2 adds Figure 6 with program-length and MSE measurements for the sum_last2 capacity sweep previously described only in prose in Appendix D. The sweep questions and ranges, unmatched-head cases, annealing analysis, and architectural interventions are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly discloses PySR random seed 42. Both versions already report means across three training seeds; there is no stated increase in repeated runs or addition of confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds accuracy, baseline, and additional-task results, including div_3 accuracy 0.67, magnetic accuracy 0.02, and continuous-task RMSEs of 4.04e-7 and 9.02e-3. Retained training losses are unchanged, and 15 retained test entries match MSE-to-RMSE conversion within rounding. The bitwise_not and bitwise_xor entries do not convert equivalently; the changed evaluation description prevents treating these as demonstrated same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces the unspecified temperature-dependent interpolation scheduler with the explicit definition alpha(tau) = (tau1 - tau)/(tau1 - tau2). This adds mathematical specificity. Other architectural equations, agreement/discrepancy definitions, and recurrence identities remain equivalent; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: a disentangled Discrete Transformer, modular algorithm extraction supporting continuous variables, and controllability through inductive biases. Comparable RNN performance and exploration-to-exploitation dynamics remain core claims; the additional evaluations principally change their supporting evidence.

C2.justification: V1's concrete limitations concerning sparse low-dimensional tasks, graded soft attention, and compression/NLU capacity are replaced by a generic trade-off statement. V2 also explicitly restricts benchmark selection to symbolically representable rules, narrows the task-formulation motivation from length invariance to position invariance, and limits the parsimony interpretation to simple instances. These materially revise applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the interpolation schedule, PySR defaults and additional ReLU operators, extraction seed 42, approximate extraction runtime, and two-decimal coefficient display. Appendix code also corrects bitwise_and input bindings from V0_input/V1_input to the V0/V1 names subsequently used. These improve documentation and code usability without establishing a new method.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the criticism that Transformer Programs merely simulate low-level operations with a distinction between bounded representations and open-form algebraic extraction. MIPS positioning emphasizes discrete latent-state approximation more precisely. The cited-work set is retained; bibliographic formatting and metadata changes do not add research coverage.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites streamline the abstract, related work, and results discussion, consolidate pruning explanations, and combine the conclusion and limitations into Conclusion and Outlook. Terminology and several headings are refined, while the main section sequence and Appendix A–E organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Table 1 as a full-width baseline/accuracy/RMSE comparison, expands and relocates Table 2 while removing its test-loss column, and adds Figure 6. The document adopts a different page template, running headers, full-width appendix prose, and reformatted code panels. V1 Figures 6–8 are retained as v2 Figures 7–9.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the central claims easier to assess through explicit program-performance/MIPS comparisons, floating-point task results, disclosed failures, and better extraction documentation. These gains outweigh the loss of concrete applicability limitations. However, much retained numerical evidence simply converts existing MSE values to RMSE, and the reduced limitations discussion tempers the overall improvement.
